subject: Latent multi-level model - please double check my syntax

messages.author: bf07198e09758e0e
messages.subject: Latent multi-level model - please double check my syntax
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’m attempting latent variable multilevel models for the first time, and I would be grateful if someone could sanity check my syntax.

The study involves a game with 10 trials for each participant. Following the game, participants complete personality ratings. I would like to see if a certain personality trait, measured as a latent variable, predicts participant responses in this game.

As I understand it, this would be a two-level random intercept model, where (L2) latent trait scores predict (L2) game responses. I’m not interested in Level 1 beyond acknowledging that game responses are nested within individuals.

Here's my attempted syntax:

mod <- '
level: 1
game_response ~~ game_response # specify variance
level: 2
# measurement mod
PERSONALITY_TRAIT =~ trait_score1 + trait_score2 + trait_score3 + trait_score4 + trait_score5 
# structural mod
game_response ~ PERSONALITY_TRAIT
'

fit_mod <- sem(model = mod, data = data, cluster = "ID", verbose = TRUE)

Does this look reasonable to people? When I run a model like this it converges and fits fairly well.

Thank you!

Best,
Hayley

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Latent multi-level model - please double check my syntax
parts: Hayley, for what it's worth, simulation studies suggest that in this situation, with exchangeable level 1 observations and the outcome at level 2, you don't lose much by simply aggregating (e.g., averaging) the level 1 values into a level 2 "observed" variable and running the resulting level-2 variables as a single-level model.
